purpose: Reconciled source purposes: [1] Define q, qc and qt as distinct canonical command/AI roles sharing common runtime dispatch and backend-alias infrastructure without collapsing their semantics into one generic model call. [2] Define `q`, `qc` and `qt` as explicit AI/model-facing command/operation surfaces with separate canonical identities and bounded responsibilities.

value.authority_rule: Reconciled source clauses: [1] Model/backend response cannot grant command or runtime authority. [2] Invoking q-family does not grant model output execution authority.
value.backend_rule: Backend/model binding is configuration and never the command semantic identity.
value.identity_rule: Each concrete member has an explicit command/operation identity.
value.namespace_rule: q-family help/metadata follows normal command registry/namespace semantics.
value.priority_rule: q has explicit non-preemptive priority within the same queue; already-running work is never preempted.
value.q_rule: `q` is the general model interaction/execution surface.
value.qc_role: code/quality/code-analysis oriented command surface with explicit target semantics
value.qc_rule: `qc` is the code/analysis-oriented model surface according to its owning profile.
value.qt_role: separate q-family role with its own declared semantics and shared alias-scoped queue behavior
value.qt_rule: `qt` is a separately declared q-family surface and does not inherit undocumented semantics from q/qc.
value.queue_rule: When resolved to the same backend alias, q/qc/qt use the same alias-scoped runtime queue.
value.shared_rule: q/qc/qt may share backend aliases and queue infrastructure without sharing command identity.
